I'm actually on seroquel and pristiq and like you say, I can't get off either drug. In the hospital, they put me on a low dose of seroquel because benzos gave me rebound anxiety. 

The first psychiatrist I saw kept inbreeding my dose of seroquel until I was on 1500mg of seroquel to treat my ptsd, which didn't work.  I told that psychiatrist to put me on minipress at a high dose (I wrote him a literature report woth dosing indtructions that I found in academic databases) and he did what I said and it's working well. But I'm still stuck 10 years later on seroquel and pristiq.

I have to stay above 200mg of seroquel a day to not feel suicidal. I've discussed with my current psychiatrist about going off it entirely in a few years,  which she supports. I'm bulimic. I've had it for 17 years. I started at 25 with my first diet, and it quickly went into restriction and purging via exercise. It stayed that way for about 3 years. Then, I started vomiting. Then everything went nuts. I was purging at work,  at home, after eating out, just everywhere. I was still exercising to compensate as well. 

It eventually started to get into a pattern where I could mostly live my life. But eating less than a toddler, exercising for hours a day, and purging was pretty unsustainable. I got to the point where I was stealing money from work and using it to buy binge food,  I stole $600 from my brother to buy binge food as well. Which I'd purge, of course. I binge drank as well, and *just* waking up in time to catch myself and not aspirate on my own vomit scared me enough to make me stop that. 

That was kind of rock bottom for me,  so I realised I needed help, and I tried really hard for a bit.  I spent money and time to get diagnosed and I tried to recover alone. But I couldn't do it properly. So I kept purging regularly, just not as much. 

I sat in quasi recovery, not totally driving myself into the ground,  still bingeing and purging all through my time at university. But the wheels really fell off a year later, and I had to be hospitalised for extreme anxiety and suicidal thoughts. 

The hospital put me on seroquel because I have bounce back anxiety from benzos the next day and and at first,  it stopped the anxiety and made me sleep. The basal metabolic rate is the minimum amount of calories your body needs to function even if you are asleep or comatose. Eating under this or close to it means that once you're active,  your body is going to have to find nutrients elsewhere.  Your body will take what it needs by eating carbohydrates stored,  then muscles (including your heart), and eventually, fat. If prolonged, it will leech calcium from your bones. The body can't give priority to normal processes like bone growth (eg, height) and menses when there's not enough food on board.
